fix(ocr): do not OCR programmatic text because a vector shape crosses it (#4209)

* fix(ocr): do not OCR programmatic text because a vector shape crosses it

The PDF-aware OCR region selector asked backends that implement
has_content_in() whether any shape or bitmap intersects a layout cluster
and sent every hit to OCR. Rules, underlines and table borders cross
clusters of perfectly good programmatic text on most documents, so on the
threaded docling-parse and pypdfium2 backends (the only ones that answer
that query) large parts of text-native pages were rasterised and OCR'd.
The classic docling-parse backend has no shape query and fell back to a
bitmap-only index, which is why the default flip to the threaded backend
in 2.123.0 (#3764) surfaced this as a CPU regression (#4174) and as worse
text in regions that already had a text layer (#4139).

Only bitmaps can now override programmatic text. Clusters with no
visible programmatic text are still OCR'd, so vector-outlined text keeps
working, and the spatial-index path no longer indexes connected shapes so
that every backend applies the same rule.

Resolves #4174

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_017KuQqvDhDkiW6n1YjhChn3
Signed-off-by: Jeff Witt <1848307+wittjeff@users.noreply.github.com>

* test(ocr): cover the spatial-index path without the removed classic backend

DoclingParseDocumentBackend is now a deprecated wrapper around the threaded
backend (#4244) and no longer supports load_page(). Drop that case and
exercise the spatial-index fallback by disabling has_content_in on the
threaded page backend instead, which still exposes connected shapes.

Signed-off-by: Jeff Witt <1848307+wittjeff@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(ocr): keep OCR-ing shapes the text layer cannot account for

Gating OCR on the mere presence of programmatic text in a cluster dropped
clusters whose text layer only covers part of them, so glyphs drawn as
filled vector paths beside real text were never recognised (reported on
#4209 with a mixed native/vector reproduction).

Shapes still do not force OCR on their own -- that is the #4174 / #4139
fix this preserves -- but a cluster is now only cleared when every shape in
it is accounted for: either a stroked segment (a rule, an underline, a
table border, as reported by get_shape_lines) or a shape with programmatic
text inside it (a highlight, a filled table cell). Stroked-vs-filled is a
structural property of the content stream rather than a heuristic, and it
separates the two cases exactly. Where a backend cannot report stroked
segments (pypdfium2 returns None), the shape's extent decides instead: a
0.8pt rule measures 145:1 long-to-thick, the stems of a 24pt vector "HI"
measure 6:1 and 1.3:1.

The shape geometry is read at most once per page and only when a cluster
carries both text and shapes, so the text-only fast path is unchanged.

Tests cover the five cases across the threaded, pypdfium2 and
spatial-index selection paths: a rule crossing text and a highlight behind
text must not OCR; vector glyphs beside native text, vector glyphs alone
and an empty region must.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Jeff Witt <1848307+wittjeff@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(ocr): require a shape's extent to agree before it counts as a rule

Building fixtures for the two edges the previous commit documented showed both
of them losing content on the default backend, and the crude extent test getting
both right where the stroked-segment report did not:

- Letterforms drawn as stroked axis-aligned segments are reported by
  get_shape_lines() exactly as a rule is, so a cluster of them was cleared.
- A rule crossing a filled glyph merges with it into one connected shape, which
  then overlaps a reported segment, so that cluster was cleared too.

Both constructions carry text the text layer does not have, so both need OCR.
The extent is now the necessary condition and the backend's report only confirms
it, which fixes both edges on docling-parse while leaving the five existing cases
unchanged: a 0.8pt rule measures 145:1 long-to-thick, vector letterforms measure
1.3:1 to 6:1 whether filled or stroked, and a rule fused with the glyph it
crosses measures 2.6:1.

This also makes the two backends agree. pypdfium2 does not implement
get_shape_lines(), and it was already deciding on extent alone -- which is why it
was the one getting these two cases right.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Jeff Witt <1848307+wittjeff@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(ocr): decide what a rule is from its extent, not a stroke report

A rule drawn as a filled rectangle -- `re f` rather than `m l S`, which plenty of
producers emit -- is never mentioned by get_shape_lines(), so requiring that
report to agree sent exactly the #4174 case back to OCR on the docling-parse
backend. pypdfium2 got it right only because it has no such report and was
already deciding on extent alone.

The stroked-segment report turns out to be wrong in both directions: it misses
filled rules, and it reports letterforms drawn as stroked segments exactly as it
reports a rule. The shape's extent alone separates every case in the fixtures, so
the report is no longer consulted and the plumbing for it is gone.

Adds the filled-rectangle rule as a third region of the edge-case fixture, since
it is the commonest of these constructions and the one whose regression would be
least visible.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Signed-off-by: Jeff Witt <1848307+wittjeff@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(ocr): judge text behind a shape only inside the cluster

A connected shape can reach far beyond the cluster it touches: an
outlined glyph fused with a page-wide fill, say. Probing the whole
shape for text then finds native text under the fill elsewhere on the
page, counts the glyph as accounted for, and the cluster is never
OCR'd. Clip the probe to the cluster first, and dismiss a sliver of a
neighbouring fill that merely crosses the cluster edge the way a rule
is dismissed.

New fixture tests/data/pdf/vector_glyphs_merged_fill.pdf pins both
constructions on the threaded, pypdfium2 and spatial-index paths.

Signed-off-by: Jeff Witt <1848307+wittjeff@users.noreply.github.com>

* fix(ocr): require text to cover a thick shape before it counts as accounted for

On a DocLayNet page an aeronautical chart drawn entirely as paths, one
connected shape, carried a single native caption in its corner. Judged
on text presence alone the chart was cleared and its vector-drawn
labels never reached OCR. Text now accounts for a shape in two ways: a
band no thicker than two text lines (a highlight, a table stripe, a
filled cell) is explained by any text on it, while a thicker shape
needs text over at least a tenth of its clipped area. Across 1,956
shape/cluster pairs in a 227-page corpus this moves 24 clusters back
to OCR, all vector figures or sparse shaded tables, and changes no
band, highlight or cell fill.

Both paths now decide from the page's text cell geometry, read lazily
on the native-query path, so the two backends agree by construction.

New fixture tests/data/pdf/vector_glyphs_in_figure.pdf pins the
figure, the band and the sidebar on all three selection paths.

Signed-off-by: Jeff Witt <1848307+wittjeff@users.noreply.github.com>

@@ -147,6 +147,18 @@ class BaseOcrModel(BasePageModel, BaseModelWithOptions):
 
     DEFAULT_DILATION_SIZE = 20
 
+    # A rule, an underline or a table border is at least this many times longer than it
+    # is thick; anything stubbier may be part of an outlined glyph. Measured on the test
+    # fixtures: a 0.8pt rule reports 145:1 stroked and 287:1 filled (pypdfium2 inflates
+    # the stroke to 2pt thick), while vector letterforms report 1.3:1 to 6:1 whether
+    # drawn filled or stroked, and a rule merged with the glyph it crosses reports 2.6:1.
+    RULE_LIKE_ASPECT_RATIO = 12.0
+    # A shape no thicker than this many text lines is a band -- a highlight, a table
+    # stripe, a filled cell -- and any text on it accounts for it.
+    THIN_SHAPE_LINE_HEIGHTS = 2.0
+    # A thicker shape is accounted for only when text covers this share of its area.
+    TEXT_BACKED_MIN_COVERAGE = 0.1
+
     # Whether the engine can run several languages at once
     multiple_languages: ClassVar[bool] = False
 
@@ -269,15 +281,120 @@ def _find_layout_ocr_rects(self, page: Page) -> list[BoundingBox]:
         )
         return ocr_rects
 
+    @staticmethod
+    def _boxes_touch(a: BoundingBox, b: BoundingBox) -> bool:
+        """Inclusive overlap test, so a zero-thickness shape segment still matches.
+
+        `BoundingBox.overlaps` is strict and reports False for a degenerate box even
+        against itself, which is precisely what a connected shape box is for a rule.
+        Both boxes must share the top-left origin the shape queries document.
+        """
+        return a.l <= b.r and b.l <= a.r and a.t <= b.b and b.t <= a.b
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _text_geometry(
+        page: Page,
+    ) -> tuple[list[BoundingBox], BoundingBoxSpatialIndex]:
+        """The page's visible text cell boxes, top-left origin, with a spatial index."""
+        assert page._backend is not None
+        assert page.size is not None
+        cells = page._backend.get_visible_text_cells()
+        if cells is None:
+            cells = page._backend.get_text_cells()
+        boxes = [
+            cell.rect.to_bounding_box().to_top_left_origin(page.size.height)
+            for cell in cells
+        ]
+        index = BoundingBoxSpatialIndex()
+        for i, box in enumerate(boxes):
+            index.insert(i, box)
+        return boxes, index
+
+    @classmethod
+    def _text_accounts_for(
+        cls,
+        probe: BoundingBox,
+        text_boxes: list[BoundingBox],
+        text_index: BoundingBoxSpatialIndex,
+    ) -> bool:
+        """Whether the text cells under `probe` explain the shape it was cut from.
+
+        A band no thicker than a couple of text lines -- a highlight, a table
+        stripe, a filled cell -- is explained by any text on it. A thicker shape
+        is explained only when text covers a fair share of its area: a chart box
+        with one native caption in a corner is not, and the labels drawn as paths
+        inside it still need OCR.
+        """
+        under = [
+            (box, area)
+            for box in (text_boxes[i] for i in text_index.intersection(probe))
+            if (area := box.intersection_area_with(probe)) > 0
+        ]
+        if not under:
+            return False
+        heights = sorted(box.height for box, _ in under)
+        line_height = heights[len(heights) // 2]
+        if min(probe.width, probe.height) <= cls.THIN_SHAPE_LINE_HEIGHTS * line_height:
+            return True
+        covered = sum(area for _, area in under)
+        return covered / probe.area() >= cls.TEXT_BACKED_MIN_COVERAGE
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def _clip_box(box: BoundingBox, clip: BoundingBox) -> BoundingBox:
+        """The part of `box` inside `clip`, for two boxes that `_boxes_touch`.
+
+        Unlike `BoundingBox.get_intersection_bbox`, a degenerate result is kept
+        rather than turned into `None`, so a shape that merely touches the clip
+        edge yields a zero-thickness box that `_is_rule_like` then dismisses.
+        """
+        return BoundingBox(
+            l=max(box.l, clip.l),
+            t=max(box.t, clip.t),
+            r=min(box.r, clip.r),
+            b=min(box.b, clip.b),
+            coord_origin=box.coord_origin,
+        )
+
+    @classmethod

fix(ocr): read PP-OCRv6 languages through rapidocr's list_supported_langs

rapidocr 3.10.0 removed the PP_OCRV6_LANGS constant from
rapidocr.utils.model_resolver. docling allows rapidocr>=3.9.1,<4.0.0, so a
fresh install now gets 3.10.0 and every RapidOCR language resolution raises
ImportError.

Read the vocabulary through list_supported_langs(TaskType.REC,
OCRVersion.PPOCRV6) instead. It exists in 3.9.1, 3.9.2 and 3.10.0 and returns
the same 52 codes.

Signed-off-by: Yihang Chen <yhc0720@berkeley.edu>

Docling Slim is a minimal-dependency version of Docling that allows you to install only the components you need. It provides the core document processing functionality with ~50MB of base dependencies, and you can add specific features through optional extras.

## When to Use Docling Slim

- **Use `docling`** (recommended): If you want the full-featured experience with all standard capabilities
- **Use `docling-slim`**: If you need fine-grained control over dependencies or want to minimize installation size

## For Most Users: Use the Main Docling Package

We recommend most users install the full-featured `docling` package instead:

```bash
pip install docling
```

The `docling` package includes all standard features, the CLI tools, and is the easiest way to get started. Visit the [main Docling documentation](https://docling-project.github.io/docling/) for complete guides and examples.

## Installation

```bash
# PDF support with local models

# PDF + CLI
```

**Lightweight SDK for parsing documents with minimal dependencies and opt-in extras**

Docling Slim is a minimal-dependency version of Docling that allows you to install only the components you need. It provides the core document processing functionality with ~50MB of base dependencies, and you can add specific features through optional extras.

## When to Use Docling Slim

- **Use `docling`** (recommended): If you want the full-featured experience with all standard capabilities
- **Use `docling-slim`**: If you need fine-grained control over dependencies or want to minimize installation size

## For Most Users: Use the Main Docling Package

We recommend most users install the full-featured `docling` package instead:

```bash
pip install docling
```

The `docling` package includes all standard features, the CLI tools, and is the easiest way to get started. Visit the [main Docling documentation](https://docling-project.github.io/docling/) for complete guides and examples.

## Installation

### With Specific Features
```bash
# PDF support with local models
pip install docling-slim[format-pdf,models-local]

# Office formats only
pip install docling-slim[format-office]

# PDF + CLI
pip install docling-slim[format-pdf,cli]

# Docling service client for using the Docling Serve API
pip install docling-slim[service-client]
```

## Available Extras

### Convenience Bundles

| Extra | Description | Use Case |
|-------|-------------|----------|
| `standard` | All standard features (same as `docling` package) | Full-featured usage |
| `all` | All available extras | Complete installation |

### CLI

| Extra | Description | Use Case |
|-------|-------------|----------|
| `cli` | Command-line interface (typer, rich) | CLI tools (docling, docling-tools) |

### Core Components

| Extra | Description | Use Case |
|-------|-------------|----------|
| `convert-core` | Core conversion components (numpy, pillow, scipy) | Basic document conversion |
| `extract-core` | Structured information extraction | Data extraction from documents |

### Format Support

#### PDF Formats

| Extra | Description | Use Case |
|-------|-------------|----------|
| `format-pdf` | PDF parsing (pypdfium2 + docling-parse) | PDF documents |
| `format-pdf-pypdfium2` | PDF rendering only | Lightweight PDF support |
| `format-pdf-docling` | Advanced PDF parsing with docling-parse (independent of pypdfium2) | Complex PDF layouts |

#### Office Formats (office = docx + pptx + xlsx)

| Extra | Description | Use Case |
|-------|-------------|----------|
| `format-office` | All Office formats | Microsoft Office documents |
| `format-docx` | Microsoft Word documents | .docx files |
| `format-pptx` | Microsoft PowerPoint | .pptx files |
| `format-xlsx` | Microsoft Excel | .xlsx files |

#### Web Formats (web = html + markdown)

| Extra | Description | Use Case |
|-------|-------------|----------|
| `format-web` | HTML and Markdown | Web content |
| `format-html` | HTML parsing | Web pages and HTML files |
| `format-markdown` | Markdown parsing | .md files |

#### Other Formats

| Extra | Description | Use Case |
|-------|-------------|----------|
| `format-latex` | LaTeX documents | .tex files |
| `format-xml-xbrl` | XBRL financial reports | Financial documents |
| `format-html-render` | HTML rendering with Playwright | Dynamic web content |
| `format-audio` | Audio transcription (Whisper) | .wav, .mp3 files |

### OCR Engines

| Extra | Description | Use Case |
|-------|-------------|----------|
| `feat-ocr-rapidocr` | RapidOCR (lightweight) | Fast OCR |
| `feat-ocr-rapidocr-onnx` | RapidOCR with ONNX runtime | Optimized OCR |
| `feat-ocr-easyocr` | EasyOCR | Multi-language OCR |
| `feat-ocr-tesserocr` | Tesseract OCR | High-accuracy OCR |
| `feat-ocr-mac` | macOS native OCR | macOS only |

### Models

| Extra | Description | Use Case |
|-------|-------------|----------|
| `models-local` | Local PyTorch models | GPU/CPU inference |
| `models-remote` | Remote model serving (Triton) | Production deployments |
| `models-onnxruntime` | ONNX Runtime acceleration | Optimized inference |
| `models-vlm-inline` | Vision Language Models | Image understanding, inline processing |

### Other features

| Extra | Description | Use Case |
|-------|-------------|----------|
| `feat-chunking` | Document chunking | RAG applications |
| `service-client` | Docling service client | Remote processing |
